blockers.analysis: The four generic except ValueError handlers surround language.term/primitive/substitute calls. Those operations invoke captured language.tick/resource tick before or during validation. A callback ValueError (not an OutsideLanguage instance) is therefore swallowed as continue/None/membership_rejections. The frozen contract allows a captured resource callback and says incomplete computation is unresolved; it does not restrict all callback failures to TimeoutError. This loses the exact policy MEMBER/definite OUT_OF_PROFILE/UNKNOWN distinction. TimeoutError happens to propagate but generic ValueError remains broader than the exported definite exclusion class.
blockers.classification: Source blocker: delegated computation failure can be misclassified as definite membership rejection
blockers.minimal_repair: Expose exact OutsideLanguage class from actual pinned language object/module, capture that exact class once in proposer, validate the exported class identity in cold caller custody, and catch only it at all four sites. Do not recognize by name/string/message or retain a ValueError fallback. All other exceptions propagate; preserve APIs/search/order/limits/bounds.
blockers.nonclaim: This is a static possible call path, not a mutation test or observed runtime failure. It does not by itself manufacture a logical fact: fresh private membership/1717 checking would still be required.
